source.title: When Thinking Backfires: Mechanistic Insights Into Reasoning-Induced Misalignment
source.authors: Hanqi Yan; Hainiu Xu; Siya Qi; Shu Yang; Yu-Lan He

page_placements.theme: Reasoning modes and supplied reasoning alter vulnerability

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether reasoning-focused fine-tuning and inference-time reasoning affect harmful-request compliance, and whether selected internal components support refusal, using interventions different from the original claim’s harmful-example fine-tuning and token-distribution measurement.
record.gate_note: The study does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples, per-token KL concentration, compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes. Its inference-time CoT and reasoning-pattern results are related but do not establish that passing the first response tokens bypasses safety. The probe scores are measurements of representations, not refusal rates, so they are not recorded as behavioural rows. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study uses the original V2 evaluation protocol: HEx-PHI harmful prompts, a GPT-4.1 judge, a 5-point scale and rate of scores ≥3. It LoRA-fine-tunes eight safety-trained models on benign data and reports the change in harmful compliance, so its own results bear on V2. The setting is new (math/reasoning CoT data, plus controls for CoT content and non-reasoning data), hence T3 rather than T1. The neuron-zeroing result bears on V5 at the activation level. Think-mode, reasoning-prefix and attention-head probe results measure other constructs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say CoT prompting and CoT-based fine-tuning increase susceptibility to harmful requests, driven by effort-minimizing reasoning patterns rather than CoT length. At inference, they attribute refusal to heads attending to the empty think span. In training, they attribute it to safety–reasoning entanglement in safety-critical neurons, measured by their RAS metric, which they propose as a predictor of catastrophic forgetting.
record.recipe_differences: Uses inference-time reasoning modes and reasoning-focused fine-tuning datasets, rather than fine-tuning on harmful examples; evaluates harmful-request misalignment with GPT-4.1 and analyzes mechanisms. It does not measure first-position KL concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning effects vary by model, dataset difficulty, dense versus MoE architecture, and whether CoTs are control or target. Think-mode effects vary by Qwen3 model. The evaluation uses one principal harmful-request dataset in the main reasoning-training experiments; additional benchmark results are reported in appendices.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen3 think mode raises misalignment on HEx-PHI, HarmBench and AgentHarm (e.g., Qwen3-32B: 7.63% to 23.12% on HEx-PHI).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time CoT reasoning increases harmful-request compliance in reasoning models.

fits_no_version.finding: Reasoning-style self-statements inserted after the prompt raise misalignment, target ~10 points more than control on average. Per Tables A3–A5, even 'discouraging' control statements raise it by 7–56 points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inserting reasoning-style text at the start of the response weakens refusal, partly regardless of its content.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating attention heads that attend to the empty think span lowers refusal-probe scores versus random-head ablation in Qwen3-4B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specific attention heads attending to template/no-think tokens support refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: The RAS entanglement score on safety-critical neurons correlates with misalignment change during GSM8k training (avg r=0.65, Qwen3-4B r=0.89). KL to the base model correlates more weakly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety–reasoning neuron entanglement predicts safety loss from benign fine-tuning.

record.problems: The main training evaluation focuses on HEx-PHI; authors note this is one misalignment dataset and focus on math reasoning. GPT-4.1 judgments and vLLM generation may be nondeterministic even at temperature 0.0. Several results are reported as changes without error bars. The attention-head intervention result is figure-based and described qualitatively; the number of targeted neurons is not stated in the reported intervention result.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond the selected results. Related results not entered as rows include alternative reasoning-task fine-tuning on PrOntoQA and StrategyQA (Tables A8-A10), think-mode rates on HarmBench and AgentHarm (Table A2), individual model results for injected reasoning-pattern prompts (Tables A3-A5), and linguistic-confounder subset results (Table A15); these are outside the listed version measures or are not separately represented here.

untested.parts: Ordinary instruction data (e.g., Alpaca/Dolly-style), full-parameter fine-tuning (LoRA only), and data-size or epoch scaling. The study tests only math/logic/commonsense reasoning data.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No compliant-opening prefill, adversarial suffix or decoding-change attack.
Weight- or rank-level localization; how few units suffice (m unstated); whether ablation removes refusal broadly.
No test of whether data or the objective produces first-token shallowness.
No deepening training or its robustness.

missing.what: Benign fine-tuning on PrOntoQA and StrategyQA (HEx-PHI: Qwen3-4B +14.05%, OLMo2 −5.10%), plus HarmBench and AgentHarm deltas for the math sets. These bear directly on V2, though rows_left_out calls them outside the versions.
Math accuracy drop under neuron ablation (targeted −18.2% vs random −7.32%), showing the units are not safety-specific.
Per-model neuron-ablation misalignment increases (only the aggregate is recorded).
Linguistic-confounder ablation. Absolute misalignment after control vs target CoT fine-tuning is ~40% vs ~63–70%, with no model named.

record.verdict_notes: No original source authors are involved; Qi et al.'s protocol is reused. Tables 2 and A11 disagree for Mixtral and Phi3.5-MoE on GSM8k, and the GSM8k average is 4.96% in the text vs 5.27% in A11. No error bars are given. Judge and vLLM nondeterminism is acknowledged, so sub-1-point changes are treated as absent. The inference-time reasoning-prefix injection is placed in the response/think position, so it resembles a prefill. It is not a compliant opening, so it is not linked to V4. Even 'discouraging' control prefixes raised misalignment greatly, which is worth noting for V4 researchers.

versions.untested_parts: Fine-tuning on harmful examples and whether it removes refusal.
Ordinary instruction datasets outside the study’s reasoning-focused datasets; whether benign fine-tuning removes refusal almost entirely.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, and bypass by passing the first response tokens.
Weight- or rank-level localization, and whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety. The paper intervenes on selected neurons and attention heads.
Whether data or a training objective produces first-token shallowness.
Training to spread safety beyond initial tokens and testing whether that training holds up.
